Crl.Misc.No.40/2021 Petitioner No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V,
 W/o Sri.Venkatesh,
 Aged about 33 years Petitioner No.2: Kum.Bhumika V  D/o Shivakumar,
 Aged about 10 years
Since 2nd petitioner is minor  represented by her Mother/ 1st  petitioner as natural guardian.

Both are R/at :No.15,
 "Varsha Nilaya",
 9th A Cross, Magadi Main Road,
 Agrahara Dasarahalli,
 Bangalore - 560 079.
(Represented by Sri.S.R.S. Adv.,)

V/s Respondent: Venkatesh S/o. Munishamappa Crl.Misc.40/2021 Aged about 38 years, R/at No.247, Hunasamarana Halli Village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk - 562 157.
(Respondent placed exparte) J UD GE M E N T
The petitioner No.1 has filed this petition U/s.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act- 2005 against the respondent.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act- 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the petitioner No.1 that she is the legally wedded wife of the respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 13.03.2009 at Muttarayana Temple, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District as per Hindu Rites and Customs and marriage expenses around Rs.1,00,000/- borne by her parents.
Further she deposed that after the marriage and respondent lived together at matrimonial house and out of the wed lock one female child born to them on 24.07.2010.

After few months of the marriage respondent started to harass her both mentally and physically and he is drunkard and used to demand the petitioner to bring dowry from her parents and threaten throw No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
1 out of the house.

Regarding the harassment, beating and demanding of dowry by the respondent on Crl.Misc.40/2021 20.12.2012 she has lodged a complaint before Yelahanka police station against the respondent and police have warned him.

Again after some time the respondent started to harass the petitioner and on demand of the respondent she brought Tata Ace goods vehicle in her name by availing loan but he never used to give any money to home nor used to pay loan EMI and insurance.
On 25.10.2019 respondent started to quarrel with her and beaten badly and abused her with filthy language and thrown her and her child out of the matrimonial home.
Further petitioner submits that now she is residing with her sister's house and her daughter is studying in 3rd standard and she is finding difficulty to lead their life.
She is working a Home Guard and earning salary of Rs.13,000/- and she is paying loan to Tata Motor finance towards TATA AC goods vehicle.

The respondent is having own house and sufficient source of income and in all he is getting Rs.25,000/-
per month, in spite of that he is failed to provide basic necessities to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioner prays for relief's as prayed in the petition.

3. After the registration of petition, notice has been issued to the respondent and the same was served on him and he remained absent as such he has placed ex-parte and hence the matter was set for trial.
Crl.Misc.40/2021 4.
In order to prove her case the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 5 documents as Ex.P.1 to 5.
Heard the counsel for petitioner.

5. The following points that arises for my consideration are as under;
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that she has been in domestic relationship with the respondent?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves that she was in a shared household along with the respondent and she has been subjected to Domestic Violence and neglected by the respondent?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs as sought in the petition?
4. What order?

POINT No.1 : In domestic violence case the petitioner has to prove the domestic relationship between the parties, she was Crl.Misc.40/2021 residing with the respondents in a shared household,
the domestic violence was caused by the respondents upon the petitioner.

The respondents No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
2 neglected the petitioner without any reasonable cause and the respondent No.1 is capable to maintain the petitioner.

8. In order to prove the aspect of her domestic relationship with respondents in her affidavit she has reiterated whatever she stated in her complaint and affirmed that she was married to respondent no.1 socially and as per Hindu rites and rituals at Sri.Muthurayan Temple, Doddaballapura on 13.03.2009 and from that period she has narrated that she has domestic relationship continuously till she she was forced to go out of matrimonial house, the petitioner has narrated that initially she set up her matrimonial home at Hunasamaranahalli Village and continued to stay their till she was forced to go out from the matrimonial home.
During her stay at Hunasamaranahalli in the matrimonial home she was having continuous domestic relationship as narrated by her with respondents.
The Respondent did not appear to rebut the evidence of the aggrieved person.
Thus from the unrebutted evidence of aggrieved person I hold that the aggrieved petitioner and the Respondent had lived together in a shared household.
Thus their relationship comes within the purview of domestic relationship as defined under the Act.
Accordingly, this court answered point No.1 in the affirmative.
Crl.Misc.40/2021 9. POINT No.2:
The petitioner claims that during her her stay period in matrimonial home at Hunasamaranahalli she was living in the shared household and subject to domestic violence in various forms.
Before proceeding further it is essential to know what is meaning of shared household and domestic violence as per the PWDV act.

In the similar manner Section 3 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 defines domestic violence as follows:
Crl.Misc.40/2021

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it-- (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
3

(b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person.

12. On the point whether the petitioner lived in shared household, as per her evidence on oath she joined the respondents in their home at Hunasamaranahalli which is their own property and there she was subjected to various forms of domestic violence in the instant case though the respondents was duly served with notice they did not appear through their counsel and has knowledge of allegations leveled against them there is no case of denial hence it can be concluded that the parties to the petition are resided in shared household, the next point is Crl.Misc.40/2021 whether the Respondents committed domestic violence on the aggrieved woman, PW1 in her evidence-on-affidavit reiterated whatever she stated in her complaint and stated that she was married with the Respondent No.1 namely in the year 2009 according to Hindu rites and rituals and led the conjugal life with him.
Out of their wedlock one female child was born to them in the year 2010.
It is stated that after consummation of marriage the respondent No.1 started to torture her verbally and mentally due to non-bringing of adequate dowry.
It is further averred that she was subjected to economic abuse as well but the petitioner continued to live in the conjugal life amid all adversities.
She has to face violation, the acts of the respondents increased upon her day by day and ultimately driven out from the matrimonial home.
Under such compelling circumstances she is currently dependent on her parents/sister.
Since last two years of her staying at paternal home, the respondent willfully neglected to maintain her in spite of having sufficient means.

She with no other option in order to provide food for herself and her daughter and in order to meet the educational expenses of the daughter she has joined Probono service of home-guard in Bengaluru and from that she is getting Rs.13,000/- per month as royalty for her services and apart from that she has no income of her own and it is specifically averred that she has the liability of the repay the vehicle loan which was borrowed by the respondent No.1 and in the name of the petitioner No.1.
She is finding very difficult for Crl.Misc.40/2021 her to maintain herself.
The respondent is working as driver and using the Tata Ace vehicle standing in the name of the petitioner No.1 and getting an income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
13. Since the respondents has not made any attempts to deny the case of petitioner by contesting the case the court has to rely on available materials on record.

From the above evidence on record in respect of point (II), it appears that the evidence of atrocities and physical/ psychological assaults upon the aggrieved woman by the respondent side is reliable and believable.
From the evidence of the aggrieved woman it appears that there were incidents of violence on the aggrieved woman by the respondents.
Since the respondent has not been able to prove that no form of violence was committed by him against the aggrieved woman.

relying on the evidence of the aggrieved woman, I hold that the aggrieved person was subjected to domestic violence in the form of physical, mental No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023
Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
4 and economic abuse by the Respondent
. In view of the above, it is seen that the aggrieved woman is succeeded to prove her case against the respondent.
It is seen that the respondent side inflicted both physical and mental torture upon the aggrieved woman and she was driven away from her matrimonial home.
Hence, the point No.2 for determination is answered in the affirmative.
Crl.Misc.40/2021 14. POINT No.3:

In the instant case, the petitioner/aggrieved has sought the following reliefs:-
I) Restraining the respondent No.1 from causing the acts of domestic violence against the petitioners.

II) Residence order U/s. 19 of the said Act, like an order directing the respondent to secure same level of alternate accommodation for the aggrieved person.
III) Monetary reliefs U/s. 20 of the said Act for maintenance amount of Rs.10,000/-
per month to petitioner NO.1 and Rs.5,000/- per month to petitioner No.2.

IV) Compensation order U/s. 22 of the said Act in terms of monetary benefit amounting to Rs.5,00,000/-.
15.

In the instant case the petitioners are claiming monetary reliefs from the respondent, she has filed assets and liability statement and shown that she is earning Rs.13,000/- per month and in their affidavit they stated opponent is working as driver and he has several source of income from rent and agricultural income.

In the instant case though the petitioners have stated their details about liabilities incurred by her parents towards performing the marriage and other activities in respect of the petitioner but they did not placed any materials to show that the Crl.Misc.40/2021 respondent is actually earning from which source to what extent, what properties are owned by him nothing is placed before the court.

Even in their assets and liabilities statement though they have given a list of assets about owning house in Hunasamaranahalli, not even a single piece of paper is placed before the court to show their allegation or contention is true.
In the instant case the respondent has knowledge of institution of petition and he received the notice of the court but he did not choose to appear and contest the case.
Even after the same he did not opt to file objection and they did not even file assets and liabilities statement.
Since the averments of the petition are in the knowledge of the respondents the court can draw adverse inference against them.

16. Hon'ble Apex court in Rajneesh V/s Neha has laid down certain guidelines to be followed while calculating the quantum of maintenance as follows;
III Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance (i) The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse.

There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
5 maintenance to be awarded.
In Manish Jain v Akanksha Jain 34 this Court held that the financial position of the parents of the applicant-wife, would not be material while determining the quantum of maintenance.
An order of interim maintenance is conditional on the circumstance that the wife or husband who makes a claim has no independent income, sufficient for her or his support.
It is no answer to a claim of maintenance that the wife is educated and could support herself.
The court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or his support.
Maintenance is dependent upon factual situations; the Court should mould the claim for maintenance based on various factors brought before it.

On the other hand, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance, and dependant family members whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would Refer to Jasbir Kaur Sehgal v District Judge, Dehradun & Ors.

entities.text: Jasbir Kaur Sehgal v District Judge, Dehradun & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Refer to Vinny Paramvir Parmar v Paramvir Parmar (2011) 13 SCC 112. (2017) 15 SCC 801.

entities.text: Vinny Paramvir Parmar v Paramvir Parmar (2011) 13 SCC 112. (2017) 15 SCC 801
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: be Crl.Misc.40/2021 required to be taken into consideration, to arrive at the appropriate quantum of maintenance to be paid.
The Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiralling inflation rates and high costs of living.
The plea of the husband that he does not possess any source of income ipso facto does not absolve him of his moral duty to maintain his wife if he is able bodied and has educational qualifications.35
(ii) A careful and just balance must be drawn between all relevant factors.

The test for determination of maintenance in matrimonial disputes depends on the financial status of the respondent, and the standard of living that the applicant was accustomed to in her matrimonial home.36

The maintenance amount awarded must be reasonable and realistic, and avoid either of the two extremes i.e. maintenance awarded to the wife should neither be so extravagant which becomes oppressive and unbearable for the respondent, nor should it be so meagre that it drives the wife to penury.
The sufficiency of the quantum has to be adjudged so that the wife is able to maintain herself with reasonable comfort.
(iii) Section 23 of HAMA provides statutory guidance with respect to the criteria for determining the quantum of maintenance.

Sub-section (2) of Section 23 of HAMA provides the following factors which may be taken into consideration :
No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
6

(i) position and status of the parties, (ii) reasonable wants of the claimant, (iii) if the petitioner/claimant is living separately, the justification for the same, (iv) value of the claimant's property and any income derived Crl.Misc.40/2021 from such property,
(v) income from claimant's own earning or from any other source.

(iv) Section 20(2) of the D.V. Act provides that the monetary relief granted to the aggrieved woman and / or the children must be adequate, fair, reasonable, and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved woman was accustomed to in her matrimonial home.

17. If the above laid down guidelines are taken into consideration the court must be conscious while awarding maintenance to aggrieved that it it should not burden the opponent as well, the court has to consider the dependents on respondent as well, in the case on hand the petitioner has not stated anything about the dependents of the respondent.
Since no objection is filed the court cannot presume on its own.
As per their pleadings the respondent is working as driver and he get around Rs.25,000 per month, but the actual amount is not stated in their assets and liabilities affidavit.
In the instant case the petitioner is claiming Rs.10,000/- towards herself and Rs.5,000/- towards daughter as maintenance amount.
In the instant case the petitioner themselves did not disclose the actual income of the respondent neither they have stated that he work as driver on his own vehicle.

The petitioner claims he get around Rs.25,000/- but the respondent also did not disclose the actual income in such circumstances the court by taking into consideration their educational qualification,
their standard of living the same is Crl.Misc.40/2021 analyzed on the basis of the area of residence where the respondents are residing.
18. With regard to the reliefs U/s.19 of the Act the petitioner is claiming the alternative accommodation of same standard which she was accustomed to in the matrimonial home.

With regard to the status since no paper is placed before the court to substantiate the contention of the petitioner the court cannot assume on its own and pass prohibitory orders as claimed by the petitioner.
On these aspects the court deny to pass any orders with regard to residential property.
However, considering all aspects and the circumstances of the case, the petitioner/aggrieved is entitled to the following reliefs, to the extent allowed:-
19 . Residence Order U/s. 19 of the said Act:

From the evidence on record it is evident that the respondents caused various modes of abuse on petitioner hence in such circumstances to let the aggrieved to reside in the shared house along with the respondent would not be safe for her,
therefore the respondent is directed to secure the same level of alternate accommodation as the aggrieved enjoyed in the shared household or pay an allowance of Rs.4,000/-(Rupees Four Thousand only) per month to the aggrieved as house rent.
Crl.Misc.40/2021 20. Monetary Reliefs U/s. 20 of the said Act:
Now, from the record it is apparent that the aggrieved has certain financial strength to provide for herself.

The aggrieved has stated that respondent is gainfully employed and his monthly income is around Rs.25,000/- p.m., but no documentary No.1: Smt.Dhanalakshmi V vs Venkatesh on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146157469/
7 evidence was brought on record to prove the same.

Having said that, it cannot be ignored that during her entire married life the petitioner was tortured by her husband and ultimately she was driven out of her home and was compelled to live in another place and fend for herself.

This Act being an beneficial legislation arms the aggrieved with an unquestionable right of maintenance as against the respondent, if she is a victim of domestic violence which can no way be defeated if she fails to precisely prove the monthly income of the respondent.
considering the educational background and family of the respondents and he being the able bodied person it is his duty to take care of wife and children.
It appears that they are capable of providing maintenance to petitioner and infant child.
Therefore the respondent is directed to pay a monthly maintenance of Rs.6,000/-(Rupees six thousand only) to the aggrieved and minor child.
21. Compensation Order U/s.22 of the said Act:
Now, the mental agony or suffering felt by the petitioner after being driven out of home in demand of dowry cannot be described in words.
The petitioner has narrated the misery which she has faced in the Crl.Misc.40/2021 matrimonial home in the hands of the respondents.
The petitioner further stated about giving of Stridhan, gold and silver articles to the respondent at the time of marriage and they are seeking return of the same.
The same in unrebutted .

Therefore considering the facts of the case, the petitioner is entitled to one time additional compensation and damages of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) for the mental torture, emotional distress and physical harassment caused to her due to acts of domestic violence of the respondent.
Hence, I answer Point No.3 partly in the affirmative.
22. POINT No.4:
In view of the materials placed before this court, pleadings, deposition and documentary evidence this court proceeds to pass the following:
OR D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is allowed in part.

Crl.Misc.40/2021

The respondent is directed to pay an amount of Rs.10,000/-p.m. (Rupees Ten thousand only) (Rs.4,000/- towards rent and Rs.6,000/- towards maintenance) to the petitioners from the date of petition till her life time or till she gets re-married whichever is earlier.
The respondent is further directed to pay an amount of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) as compensation to the petitioner.

The respondent is further directed to pay an amount of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) as compensation to the petitioner.
Office is directed to furnish a copy of this order free of cost to the petitioner.
